title: FDA Expands Frozen Berry Recall to Eight States After E. Coli Outbreak
excerpt: Publix has pulled GreenWise frozen blueberries and mixed berries from shelves across the Southeast after 12 people were sickened by E. coli O145.
body:
• Publix recalled frozen GreenWise organic blueberries and mixed berries across eight states after an E. coli O145 outbreak sickened 12 people
  • Four patients have been hospitalized; no deaths have been reported, with cases ranging from age 2 to 88
  • The recalled products were distributed to stores in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Virginia
  • The berries were packed by a Chilean company, Frutas y Hortalizas del Sur S.A., and the FDA investigation remains ongoing

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has expanded a recall of frozen berries sold at Publix grocery stores across eight states after an E. coli outbreak linked to the products sickened 12 people, four of whom required hospitalization.

On July 29, Publix recalled all lots of frozen GreenWise Organic Whole Blueberries and Whole Mixed Berries, broadening an earlier recall that covered only a single lot of blueberries. The products were shipped to Publix stores in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Virginia.

The Outbreak

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention identified 12 people infected with E. coli O145, a Shiga toxin-producing strain that can cause severe illness including bloody diarrhea and a potentially life-threatening kidney condition called hemolytic uremic syndrome. Patients ranged from 2 to 88 years of age.

Eleven of the 12 confirmed cases were in Florida, with one in Georgia. Symptoms among those sickened developed between May 11 and June 5. No deaths have been reported.

Investigators linked the berries to the outbreak after interviewing patients: of nine people questioned, seven — roughly 78 percent — reported eating frozen blueberries, far above the 24 percent baseline in national dietary surveys. DNA fingerprinting confirmed the bacterial strains from patients were genetically closely related.

Source Traced to Chile

The initial recall on July 3 was initiated by Frutas y Hortalizas del Sur S.A., a grower-packer based in San Carlos, Chile, that operates under the Comfrut brand. The recalled product was frozen GreenWise Organic IQF Blueberries in 10-ounce bags, lot code 60401, with a best-by date of February 9, 2028.

The expanded July 29 recall covers all lots of both blueberry and mixed berry products, suggesting the contamination may extend beyond a single production run.

What Consumers Should Do

The FDA and CDC are urging consumers across all eight states to check their freezers and discard any recalled products or return them for a refund. Surfaces and containers that may have touched the berries should be cleaned with hot soapy water or run through a dishwasher.

The investigation remains ongoing, and the FDA has said it will update its advisory as more information becomes available, including whether the berries were distributed to retailers beyond Publix.

For Indian-American families and the broader diaspora in the southeastern United States, the recall is a reminder to check freezer stocks and monitor the FDA's updates, particularly during summer months when frozen berries are a common staple.
